acceptance_criteria.observable: From a clean product baseline, public `npm ci`, UI typecheck, UI production build, Python checks, and Signoff scope verification pass without untracked generated dependency/build/cache outputs, and the sealed Signoff patch receipt contains no `.signoff` control artifacts.

oracle.description: Command evidence proves npm install/typecheck/build and Python repo checks pass; generated-output status shows dependency/build/cache outputs are ignored; the conformance suite inspects sealed PATCH.diff for `.signoff` paths.

constraints: Preserve unrelated user work and existing behavior outside the goal
Keep Python runtime dependencies at zero
Preserve the one-path non-technical installation experience
Do not change UI behavior, package manager, install flow, services, provider routing, or protocol semantics beyond applying existing control-path filtering consistently
Add or keep an adversarial conformance test before changing receipt filtering
non_goals: UI redesign or frontend feature work
New package managers, services, Docker, databases, authentication, cloud infrastructure, or runtime dependencies
Dependency upgrades, version changes, broad cleanup, formatting churn, or agent quorum changes

requirements.statement: Make contributor UI first-run install reproducible from the public npm lockfile, keep generated outputs ignored, and ensure Signoff patch receipts exclude control artifacts

stop_conditions: Stop if public npm install remains blocked by external registry or network state after lockfile normalization
Pivot if receipt correctness requires a protocol semantic change rather than consistent application of existing control-path filtering
Stop if proof requires private credentials, private registries, or committing generated outputs
Stop if the patch needs files outside the locked contract
